title: $\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k,\sigma}$ is isomorphic to $\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k}$
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $X$ be a smooth projective curve over $k$ with
a $k$-rational point $\sigma$. Then the functors
$\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k,\sigma}$ and
$\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k}$ on
$(\mathit{Sch}/k)_{fppf}$ are isomorphic. In particular
$\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k,\sigma}$ is an fppf sheaf (represented once $\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k}$ is;
and covariantly: if $\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k,\sigma}$ is representable, then so is
$\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k}$, by the group law of [thm-pc-pic-split]).

proof.text: By [lem-pc-rational-hyp], the rational-point curve satisfies the section and pushforward hypotheses of [thm-pc-pic-split].

By [thm-pc-pic-split], Pic_{X/k} is the fppf sheafification of the presheaf K(T)=Ker(σ_T^*), and by [lem-pc-k-sheaf] the presheaf K is itself an fppf sheaf; since Pic_{X/k,σ}=K by [def-pc-pic-sigma-functor], the canonical inclusion followed by sheafification is a natural isomorphism of functors.

A functor naturally isomorphic to a representable functor is representable, by transporting the Yoneda element across the natural isomorphism. Since the isomorphism of step 2 goes both ways, $\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k,\sigma}$ is representable once $\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k}$ is, and conversely $\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k}$ is representable once $\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k,\sigma}$ is; the group structure of $K(T)=\operatorname{Ker}\sigma_T^*\subset\operatorname{Pic}(X_T)$ from [thm-pc-pic-split] is compatible with the isomorphism and so transports to the representing object.
